{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && cat > HANDOFF.md <<'EOF'
# HANDOFF - 001-transactions (tinydb BatchWriter)

## Status: specify phase COMPLETE (2026-10-17)
- SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY=/testbed/specs/001-transactions; SPEC_FILE=specs/001-transactions/spec.md
- .specify/feature.json -> {"feature_directory": "specs/001-transactions"}
- No .specify/extensions.yml -> no before/after hooks to run.

## Active requirements (all retained; none replaced)
- M1: R01 apply() ops list, insert/remove, returns inserted IDs, [] for empty, ValueError malformed.
- M1: R02 atomic batch, rollback full pre-batch default-table data, missing remove ID = error, pre-acquired handles reflect success+rollback.
- M1: R03 ordinary APIs intact, no aliasing (deep-copy input), post-apply mutation of op cannot mutate db.
- M2: R04 reject bool doc_id; structural pre-commit validation; ValueError for unsupported fields / non-list ops / non-dict documents; accept {} documents.
- M2: R05 preview(ops) returns would-be inserted IDs, zero side effects incl. on error; preview + failed apply must NOT consume IDs; handles/query caches coherent.
- M2: R06 direct db.insert between calls must be seen; no stale snapshot caching.
- Claim-A: R05b preview returns new detached list each call; mutating returned list affects nothing.
- Claim-A r2: R05 clarification - successful apply advances next-insertion-ID state and writes it back to the underlying table; subsequent inserts (apply or direct db.insert) continue sequence without reuse/rewind, even across removes.

## Conflict resolution (recorded in spec.md 'Conflicting Evidence - Resolved')
- Older note 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted' = UNVERIFIED, SUPERSEDED by R04/R05. Do not rely on it.
- Happy-path smoke alone does not verify boundaries; dedicated tests required (SC-006..SC-008).

## Design anchors verified in repo (evidence from tinydb/table.py inspection)
- Table._get_next_id(): if _next_id is None -> max(existing ids)+1 (empty table -> 1); else cursor+1. So after rollback, resetting table._next_id=None makes next insert = max+1 = pre-batch next ID (failed apply consumes nothing). After successful batch, set _next_id = max(pre_batch_max, max inserted)+1 and it persists via storage (direct db.insert sees it).
- Table.insert (plain dict) never resets _next_id -> direct inserts continue wrapper's persisted cursor (no rewind). Document-class inserts do reset to None (max-based) - still no reuse.
- Table.remove(doc_ids=...) silently skips missing IDs -> wrapper must pre-check membership (str(doc_id) in table) and raise ValueError for missing.
- Table._update_table: storage holds whole DB; _read_table re-reads storage every call -> no stale snapshot if wrapper reads storage per call (R06).
- Table.search() uses _query_cache; Table.clear_cache() (public) clears it -> call on rollback so pre-acquired handles' cached queries stay coherent.
- Table.insert stores dict(document) (shallow) -> wrapper must deepcopy operations before insert and return deepcopy of stored docs (R03 no-aliasing).
- Storage JSON keys are strings; compare with str(doc_id).

## Spec structure (specs/001-transactions/spec.md, 166 lines)
- US1 apply (P1), US2 atomic rollback (P1), US3 transparency/no-aliasing (P2), US4 preview purity (P1), US5 ID sequencing across mixed usage (P2).
- FR-001..FR-009 + FR-004a (preview), FR-004b (ID state advance+persist), FR-004c (no stale snapshot).
- SC-001..SC-008; 9 assumptions; conflict section; checklist checklists/requirements.md all [x] incl. milestone-2 update block.
- 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers.

## Implementation contract for next phases
- New file tinydb/journal.py: class BatchWriter(db) with apply(operations)->list[int], preview(operations)->list[int]; default table only; ValueError on all malformed/missing cases; deepcopy isolation; snapshot+restore rollback; _next_id management per above; clear_cache() on rollback.
- Own tests: tests/test_journal.py. Upstream tests unchanged. Public gate: acceptance_public.py (imports tinydb.journal; tests basic/atomic/preview).
- Test command: python3 -m pytest -o addopts="" tests/ acceptance_public.py -q (baseline pre-impl: 223 passed in 1.28s).
EOF
python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('.specify/feature.json')))"; wc -l HANDOFF.md"}
